key_insight: PhySGA improves 3D object composition by combining LLM-style planning with physics-grounded simulation feedback for interactive, physically plausible assembly.
engineering_relevance: This framework is relevant for digital content creation and robot simulation because it can handle complex tasks like hanging, settling, and containment that require closed-loop physical reasoning.
method: Assembly Agent plans global steps and coarse geometric/kinematic adjustments.
Critic Agent diagnoses simulator state using contact dynamics for fine-grained correction.
Action Routers convert semantic plans into executable simulator primitives, and a Self-Evolving Skill Library reuses prior trial-and-error experience.
evidence_signal: In Isaac Sim experiments, the method is reported to outperform prior approaches on relation fidelity, physical plausibility, and visual quality.
watch_item: Performance likely depends on simulator fidelity and the quality of closed-loop exploration, which may limit transfer to real-world or out-of-simulation settings.
paper_title: PhySGA: A Physics-Space Grounded Agentic Framework for Generalizable and Interactive 3D Composition
